svg.aria-label: The map of Rerail 0.1.5: every part that runs and every link between them, each arrow from the part that waits to the part it waits on, with the number of clocks on each.
svg.title: The map of Rerail 0.1.5: every part that runs and every link between them, each arrow from the part that waits to the part it waits on, with the number of clocks on each.

rect.title: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor (hooks) and OMP, Pi (extensions in the agent's own process). Not Rerail's code; it starts every hook and waits for its answer.
Claude Code runs it at each refresh: reads the checkout's state from the daemon, or the database read-only when no daemon answers.
A process the agent starts for Rerail's MCP tools: reads daemon.json, proves the daemon on Windows, relays each JSON-RPC call to the daemon's HTTP API.
Runs inside the agent: attaches a native session to the daemon, holds a tool call while its check runs (25 s budget), polls for background steers every 100 ms, renews a 60 s lease by every request.
A page in the browser served by the daemon. Polls each resource every 5 s with If-None-Match, backs off to 30 s while the daemon is unreachable, pauses while the tab is hidden.

rerail start, stop, status, session, scan, daemon start and stop, setup, install, update, uninstall, scrub, reset, support-bundle. Each runs as its own node process and talks to the daemon over HTTP, to the database directly, and to npm, Git, gh and PowerShell as children.

rerail setup, install, update and uninstall: register the hooks in each coding agent's settings and check them by running one, install rule packs with npm under the packs lock, write the set-up stores (SQLite) and the shell PATH; update stops the daemon, installs the new version and starts it.
Dev daemon scripts (just rerail-dev, rerail --restore, rerail-smoke), the cloud test matrix and its guests, release and upstream scripts. Not shipped to users.
vitest suites (test/, integration/, e2e/, benchmark/) and the engine's cargo tests.

The command the agent runs for each event: on macOS and Linux `sh -c 'if [ -x "$0" ]; then exec "$0" "$1"; fi; exec node "$1"'` (exec, so node replaces sh); on Windows PowerShell for Codex and Cursor, and for Claude Code the hook launcher, a small node script that runs the hook under the recorded node, in its own process or as a child.

One node process per event: reads the event on stdin, checks whether Rerail is on in the folder, finds the daemon (starting one when none runs), takes the session's lock, sends the event to the engine socket and prints the answer.

daemon.json (the daemon's address and capability), daemon.lock and its holder record, the start lock and the autostart claim under locks/, the port and access token files, daemon.log, the hook failure log, the session lock files under the storage root.

rerail.sqlite (sessions, events, audits, rules, start rows) opened by the daemon on its main thread with a 5 s busy timeout, read-only by hooks and the status line, written by commands (reset, scrub, set-up). Also the set-up stores, the remote outbox and the provenance move's worker thread.

One node process per Rerail home. Its single JavaScript thread answers every hook, the HTTP API, the dashboard and native sessions. Holds the home daemon lock and, for the installed build, the machine's main-instance lock; writes daemon.json once it listens; restarts itself near its heap ceiling.

An HTTP server on a Unix socket or a Windows named pipe inside the daemon. Takes POST /events, routes each event to its checkout's runtime through a per-session queue, answers with the deliveries (blocks, steers). Sweeps quiet sessions every 60 s, retires a checkout's runtime 15 min after its last session.

A RerailRuntime per checkout holds its sessions: records each event in the database, opens the session's code rules, checks edits, walks the session's checkout after shell commands, waits for checks at a turn's end, runs Merge Assist.

The session walk reads the checkout after a shell command (10 s cap). The worktree walk reads a repository's other worktrees once for all sessions, paced at 5 s, with a full walk every 10 min, fed by the engine's tree watch (inotify, FSEvents, ReadDirectoryChangesW with oplocks).

Code-rule evaluation, one at a time per daemon (a second is refused with WORKSPACE_BUSY), a 5 ms inline budget on the JavaScript thread, the module graph, the tree watch thread, the main-instance and home file locks (try-only), the Windows detached spawn.
Git (10 s limit per call), npm (3 min per query, 20 min per install), gh (20 s per run), the person's own conflict hook (10 s by default), PowerShell, icacls, whoami, scutil, the Orca CLI.

One SQLite file per machine for the installed build (a checkout's own for a dev build). Every writer is a thread of the main daemon. A maintenance thread wakes every 30 s: renews workspace leases, collects when over capacity, builds search indexes for up to 1 s.

svg.text: Daemon process, one per Rerail home
One JavaScript thread answers every hook and request

g.title: L01: Coding agent waits on Hook entry. a child process per event: the event as JSON on stdin, the answer on stdout. the agent waits for the hook's exit; on Windows a hook whose parent was killed ends itself by a 1 s check

L01: Coding agent waits on Hook entry. a child process per event: the event as JSON on stdin, the answer on stdout. the agent waits for the hook's exit; on Windows a hook whose parent was killed ends itself by a 1 s check
L02: Hook entry waits on Hook process. exec on macOS and Linux (one process); a child process on Windows (PowerShell, cmd.exe or the launcher's spawnSync). the entry waits for the hook's exit
L02: Hook entry waits on Hook process. exec on macOS and Linux (one process); a child process on Windows (PowerShell, cmd.exe or the launcher's spawnSync). the entry waits for the hook's exit

L03: Hook process waits on Rerail database and the other SQLite files. a read-only SQLite open per hook (the checkout's start rows); two writable opens per delivered steer (its receipt). the hook waits on SQLite's lock (5 s busy timeout per open)

L03: Hook process waits on Rerail database and the other SQLite files. a read-only SQLite open per hook (the checkout's start rows); two writable opens per delivered steer (its receipt). the hook waits on SQLite's lock (5 s busy timeout per open)
L04: Hook process waits on Daemon process. HTTP reads of the daemon's API (start state, dashboard address, checkout scope, rule count), 2 s each. the hook waits for each answer up to 2 s
L04: Hook process waits on Daemon process. HTTP reads of the daemon's API (start state, dashboard address, checkout scope, rule count), 2 s each. the hook waits for each answer up to 2 s

L05: Hook process waits on Rerail home files. daemon.json read, the start lock and autostart claim (files under locks/), a detached `rerail daemon start` when none runs. the hook polls the lock every 50 ms up to 15 s, a record every 100 ms up to 15 s

L05: Hook process waits on Rerail home files. daemon.json read, the start lock and autostart claim (files under locks/), a detached `rerail daemon start` when none runs. the hook polls the lock every 50 ms up to 15 s, a record every 100 ms up to 15 s

L06: Hook process waits on Engine service (the answering socket). a Unix socket or named pipe: the capability proof (Windows), then POST /events; the answer carries blocks and steers. the hook waits for the daemon: 2 s probe, then the rest of 12 s from its arrival, then 30 s of socket silence on the request

L06: Hook process waits on Engine service (the answering socket). a Unix socket or named pipe: the capability proof (Windows), then POST /events; the answer carries blocks and steers. the hook waits for the daemon: 2 s probe, then the rest of 12 s from its arrival, then 30 s of socket silence on the request

L07: Hook process waits on Hook process. the session's lock file, shared by parallel hooks of one session. a waiter polls every 10 ms up to 30 s; a holder silent 10 s is taken over; the holder touches the file every 1 s

L07: Hook process waits on Hook process. the session's lock file, shared by parallel hooks of one session. a waiter polls every 10 ms up to 30 s; a holder silent 10 s is taken over; the holder touches the file every 1 s
L08: Hook process waits on Rerail home files. the hook failure log (one line per lost event). nobody; a rename retried for 2 s on Windows
L08: Hook process waits on Rerail home files. the hook failure log (one line per lost event). nobody; a rename retried for 2 s on Windows

L09: Commands a person runs waits on Daemon process. HTTP probes (/healthz, 2 s), POST /native/shutdown (Windows, 2 s), signals; scan requests and reads. the command waits for the answer, then for the daemon's exit by a 100 ms poll

L09: Commands a person runs waits on Daemon process. HTTP probes (/healthz, 2 s), POST /native/shutdown (Windows, 2 s), signals; scan requests and reads. the command waits for the answer, then for the daemon's exit by a 100 ms poll

L10: Commands a person runs waits on Daemon process. the launch: a detached spawn, then daemon.json and /healthz read every 100 ms; on Windows the exit code read every 100 ms. the launcher waits up to 15 s for ready

L10: Commands a person runs waits on Daemon process. the launch: a detached spawn, then daemon.json and /healthz read every 100 ms; on Windows the exit code read every 100 ms. the launcher waits up to 15 s for ready

L11: Daemon process waits on Rerail home files. daemon.json written once it listens and checked every 1 s; the home daemon lock (1 s wait at start); the main-instance lock. a second daemon polls the home lock every 50 ms for 1 s

L11: Daemon process waits on Rerail home files. daemon.json written once it listens and checked every 1 s; the home daemon lock (1 s wait at start); the main-instance lock. a second daemon polls the home lock every 50 ms for 1 s

L12: Engine service (the answering socket) waits on Sessions and their runtime. in-process calls through a per-session queue (one event at a time per session); a 60 s sweep of quiet sessions; a 15 min timer per idle checkout runtime; 1 s looks for stalled requests at close. each event waits for the events of its session ahead of it

L12: Engine service (the answering socket) waits on Sessions and their runtime. in-process calls through a per-session queue (one event at a time per session); a 60 s sweep of quiet sessions; a 15 min timer per idle checkout runtime; 1 s looks for stalled requests at close. each event waits for the events of its session ahead of it
L13: Status line waits on Daemon process. an HTTP read of the presentation (2 s), else the database read-only. Claude Code waits for the status command up to its 2 s
L13: Status line waits on Daemon process. an HTTP read of the presentation (2 s), else the database read-only. Claude Code waits for the status command up to its 2 s

L14: Sessions and their runtime waits on Engine (Rust, loaded into node). napi calls: apply an edit, evaluate, open a workspace; inline on the JavaScript thread up to 5 ms, else on a pool thread; one evaluation at a time, a second refused and retried. a check waits for the evaluation ahead (retries 2 to 25 ms apart); the answer waits for checks up to 1 s (hooks) or 10 s (OMP, Pi)

L14: Sessions and their runtime waits on Engine (Rust, loaded into node). napi calls: apply an edit, evaluate, open a workspace; inline on the JavaScript thread up to 5 ms, else on a pool thread; one evaluation at a time, a second refused and retried. a check waits for the evaluation ahead (retries 2 to 25 ms apart); the answer waits for checks up to 1 s (hooks) or 10 s (OMP, Pi)

L15: Engine (Rust, loaded into node) waits on Content store and its maintenance thread. SQLite write transactions from the apply's publication, the attach's batches, lease renewals and collection; reads through a 32 MiB cache. a writer polls SQLite's lock 1 to 100 ms apart, 250 ms per attempt, up to 10 s; then the store is skipped for 30 s

L15: Engine (Rust, loaded into node) waits on Content store and its maintenance thread. SQLite write transactions from the apply's publication, the attach's batches, lease renewals and collection; reads through a 32 MiB cache. a writer polls SQLite's lock 1 to 100 ms apart, 250 ms per attempt, up to 10 s; then the store is skipped for 30 s

L16: Sessions and their runtime waits on Rerail database and the other SQLite files. SQLite writes on the daemon's one JavaScript thread (events, sessions, steers, audits); the provenance move's worker thread. a write waits up to 5 s for another process's transaction, holding every hook behind it; a 250 ms poll of scan requests and settings

L16: Sessions and their runtime waits on Rerail database and the other SQLite files. SQLite writes on the daemon's one JavaScript thread (events, sessions, steers, audits); the provenance move's worker thread. a write waits up to 5 s for another process's transaction, holding every hook behind it; a 250 ms poll of scan requests and settings
L17: Sessions and their runtime waits on Child programs. Git as child processes (10 s each; the end read by a 1 s tick; 500 ms for output held open). the session waits for Git's exit
L17: Sessions and their runtime waits on Child programs. Git as child processes (10 s each; the end read by a 1 s tick; 500 ms for output held open). the session waits for Git's exit

L18: Walks and the tree watch waits on Engine (Rust, loaded into node). the tree watch thread's notices, taken by a 250 ms poll; walks paced 5 s apart; a full walk every 10 min; the Windows watch reopened 200 ms after a rename. nobody waits on the background walks; the session walk holds a shell command's result and a turn end up to 10 s

L18: Walks and the tree watch waits on Engine (Rust, loaded into node). the tree watch thread's notices, taken by a 250 ms poll; walks paced 5 s apart; a full walk every 10 min; the Windows watch reopened 200 ms after a rename. nobody waits on the background walks; the session walk holds a shell command's result and a turn end up to 10 s
L19: Dashboard waits on Daemon process. HTTP conditional GETs every 5 s; setting writes (30 s limit); keep-alive connections (5 s idle). the page waits for the next poll to show a change
L19: Dashboard waits on Daemon process. HTTP conditional GETs every 5 s; setting writes (30 s limit); keep-alive connections (5 s idle). the page waits for the next poll to show a change

L20: OMP and Pi extension waits on Daemon process. HTTP to /native/*: attach, events with deferred replies (answered by 10 s), a poll every 100 ms, a 60 s lease renewed by each request, close. the extension holds a tool call up to 25 s; a request waits up to 30 s, an operation up to 120 s

L20: OMP and Pi extension waits on Daemon process. HTTP to /native/*: attach, events with deferred replies (answered by 10 s), a poll every 100 ms, a 60 s lease renewed by each request, close. the extension holds a tool call up to 25 s; a request waits up to 30 s, an operation up to 120 s

L21: MCP bridge waits on Daemon process. the agent's MCP calls on stdio, relayed as HTTP; a 2 s proof on Windows and a 2 s /healthz on the first call. the agent's tool call waits for the relay up to 30 s

L21: MCP bridge waits on Daemon process. the agent's MCP calls on stdio, relayed as HTTP; a 2 s proof on Windows and a 2 s /healthz on the first call. the agent's tool call waits for the relay up to 30 s
L22: Daemon process waits on Child programs. child processes the daemon starts: the TLS key reader, icacls, PowerShell, whoami, scutil, the Orca CLI. the daemon's start waits for each child's answer
L22: Daemon process waits on Child programs. child processes the daemon starts: the TLS key reader, icacls, PowerShell, whoami, scutil, the Orca CLI. the daemon's start waits for each child's answer

L23: Sessions and their runtime waits on Child programs. Merge Assist in the daemon: gh, Git and the person's conflict hook as children; a 5 min gh cache; a 30 s window between passes. an edit's result waits up to 1 s for the pass's note

L23: Sessions and their runtime waits on Child programs. Merge Assist in the daemon: gh, Git and the person's conflict hook as children; a 5 min gh cache; a 30 s window between passes. an edit's result waits up to 1 s for the pass's note

L24: Daemon process waits on Rerail database and the other SQLite files. the remote sink (an experiment): its outbox SQLite file, the Rerail database read-only, HTTPS to a remote. nobody waits; a 10 s tick, backoff up to 5 min

L24: Daemon process waits on Rerail database and the other SQLite files. the remote sink (an experiment): its outbox SQLite file, the Rerail database read-only, HTTPS to a remote. nobody waits; a 10 s tick, backoff up to 5 min

L25: Set-up and update waits on Child programs. set-up, update, install, uninstall: npm and the registry, the packs folder lock, PowerShell, the registered hooks, the set-up stores (SQLite). the person waits at the command; each child has a limit

L25: Set-up and update waits on Child programs. set-up, update, install, uninstall: npm and the registry, the packs folder lock, PowerShell, the registered hooks, the set-up stores (SQLite). the person waits at the command; each child has a limit

L26: Commands a person runs waits on Rerail home files. renames and removals of files another program may hold open (Windows): replaceFile, removeWithRetry, the clock-sample folder. the caller retries 50 ms to 1 s apart, up to 2 to 10 s

L26: Commands a person runs waits on Rerail home files. renames and removals of files another program may hold open (Windows): replaceFile, removeWithRetry, the clock-sample folder. the caller retries 50 ms to 1 s apart, up to 2 to 10 s

L27: Commands a person runs waits on Rerail database and the other SQLite files. rerail scrub, reset, project and uninstall writing or reading the database beside a running daemon. the command waits on SQLite's lock (5 to 10 s)

L27: Commands a person runs waits on Rerail database and the other SQLite files. rerail scrub, reset, project and uninstall writing or reading the database beside a running daemon. the command waits on SQLite's lock (5 to 10 s)
L30: Daemon process waits on Daemon process. the restart at the heap ceiling: the heap read every 30 s, then a relaunch with the same arguments. hooks wait through the new daemon's start
L30: Daemon process waits on Daemon process. the restart at the heap ceiling: the heap read every 30 s, then a relaunch with the same arguments. hooks wait through the new daemon's start
